text:
Bitcoin remained bound in a low-volume consolidation range of $60,800–$61,500 midday June 25, suppressed by an abysmal Fear & Greed reading of 12. Digital asset markets are currently weathering a seventh consecutive week of institutional ETF outflows, leaving price discovery largely paralyzed. Meanwhile, the global regulatory vise continues to tighten; ahead of the July 1 EU MiCA deadline, only an estimated 210 out of 3,000 crypto firms have secured full authorization, forcing rapid industry consolidation while Dubai’s VARA intensifies penalties on unlicensed entities.

This crypto hesitation directly reflects an ambiguous macroeconomic environment. While a massive Micron Technology earnings beat briefly revived semiconductor equities, a surprise 7.3% plunge in U.S. new home sales exposed structural weakness. Consequently, the U.S. Treasury yield curve flattened as sovereign bond yields retreated globally, signaling that institutional capital is adopting a strictly defensive posture ahead of imminent PCE inflation data.
